newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees better British ties - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees better British ties - agency.

text.p: Russia expects the new British government of Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair to continue to improve relations between Moscow and London, a senior foreign ministry official told Interfax news agency on Friday.

"During the period of John Major's premiership, relations between Russian and Great Britain moved to a qualitatively new level," the official said. "Labour's manifesto positions allow us to consider that the capital of Russo-British relations will not only be conserved but increased."
Officials, continuing their May Day holiday, were not available for comment. Interfax said Russia would send its congratulations to Blair once his victory was fully confirmed.

Major took over as prime minister in 1990, a year before the Soviet Union collapsed. His right-wing predecessor, Margaret Thatcher, had forged an unprecedented working relationship with reforming Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev. She remains an icon for some Russian liberals.

Yegor Gaidar, who imposed sweeping deregulation and privatisation as Russian prime minister from 1991 to 1992, told Ekho Moskvy radio that Blair had "broken with those stupid habits of extending state control".

Blair, whose party won a massive majority on Thursday after 18 years in opposition, has moved Labour away from the left wing socialist policies that prompted accusations by opponents that some of its leaders had Kremlin sympathies during the Cold War.
